notes:
Background: Supportly builds a chat-first support layer used by SaaS mid-market customers. They want to replace mixed vendor stack (current: vendorX for NLU + homegrown streaming proxy). Primary driver: consistent sub-1.5s first-token SLO for support agents and lower token costs.

Key technical requirements (from CTO Lina Gomez):
- Streaming required for agent UI (partial tokens/turn-by-turn).
- First-token SLO: median <1.0s, 95th <1.5s — "If we can't guarantee <1.5s FT, we can't flip production".
- Tool-calling: must support CRM lookup + calendar query as function-call style (low overhead, <500ms extra).
- Throughput: baseline 5k concurrent chats across region, peak bursts to 12k.
- Latency during cold-starts and KV cache priming is a major concern.
- Cost sensitivity: target unit costs to beat current contract (their benchmark ~ $220 per 1M tokens).

Security/compliance notes:
- Must be SOC2 + SSO/SAML + audit logs.
- EU data residency for specific customers; POC will use NA but Dedicated proposal must include option for EU VPC.

POC scope & success criteria (agreed):
- 2-week hosted API POC, streaming enabled, instrumented latency tracing.
- Metric targets: first-token median <1.0s, 95th <1.5s; avg token cost goal <$200 per 1M tokens; error rate <0.5%.
- Function-call test: CRM lookup end-to-end <500ms added latency (measured).
- Quality: assist accuracy on 300-shot evaluation set >= baseline vendor accuracy.

Recent notes from SE (Maya):
- Ran quick test with VendorX + our prototype: observed FT ~1.8s median under similar load. Redwood demo recorded FT ~1.2s with streaming and prefix caching; they want side-by-side during POC.
- Need to confirm model variant (quantized vs fp16) that satisfies quality/latency tradeoff for streaming.

Commercials & timeline:
- Interested in Hosted POC immediately; potential move to 6-12 month Dedicated commit if POC passes.
- ARR ask: rough $60k-$120k depending on committed throughput and EU option.

Customer quote from CTO on 2026-01-20 call: "We need predictable first-packet latency — customer experience drops off if agents wait. Show us numbers, we'll move."
